sources.entry: Rapidbay - Videostreaming service/torrent client that allows searching and playing videos from torrents in the browser or from a Chromecast/AppleTV/Smart TV. MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: RapidBay is a self-hosted web app that searches torrent indexers and turns selected videos into browser- or Chromecast-playable streams.
summary.what_it_does: It uses Jackett and/or Prowlarr as a search backend, with results merged and deduplicated when both are configured. Users pick individual video files from a torrent, and the app downloads and converts them into a streamable format. It automatically fetches subtitles from OpenSubtitles.org and converts video, subtitles, and unsupported audio (to AAC) so they play across browsers, Chromecast, and Apple TV. It can register as a handler for magnet links and removes its own disk usage automatically. The README also mentions Kodi support and optional debrid caching through Real Debrid and TorBox.
use_cases: stream torrent videos in a browser
cast torrent movies to Chromecast or Apple TV
search torrent indexers for video content
automatically download subtitles for torrented videos
self-hosted torrent streaming on a home server
play magnet links from a web interface
how_to_run: docker run -p 5000:5000 -e JACKETT_HOST="<your Jackett URL>" -e JACKETT_API_KEY="YourAPIKey" hauxir/rapidbay
docker run -p 5000:5000 -e PROWLARR_HOST="<your Prowlarr URL>" -e PROWLARR_API_KEY="YourAPIKey" hauxir/rapidbay
sudo apt install python3 python3-venv ffmpeg mediainfo nginx
notable: Accepts both Jackett and Prowlarr as search backends and merges their results
Converts video, subtitles and unsupported audio so files play on most devices
Registers as a default handler for magnet links via /registerHandler
Optional debrid caching with Real Debrid, falling back to TorBox
caveats: Subtitle downloads require a VIP account at OpenSubtitles.org
Requires a separately running Jackett or Prowlarr indexer for search
Non-Docker setup needs ffmpeg, mediainfo and nginx installed on the host
